title: Formal Algebraic and F2-Circuit Certification for the NP-Completeness of Optimal CNOT Synthesis on Linear Oracles
abstract: We present a machine-checked constructive Lean 4.35.0 kernel and zero-float F_2 circuit verification suite (CNOT-HARD-CERT-1.0) auditing Andreas Pavlogiannis's proof that optimal CNOT synthesis is NP-complete even for involutive linear oracles B_G and even with free SWAP gates or ancillas (arXiv:2611.34138v1). Our artifact combines 18 constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings), an AST-audited zero-float Python F_2 bitmask verifier, 16 canonical JSON certificates (C01-C16), and 36 unit and forgery-rejection tests. In Lean we formalize linear-oracle involution, 3-CNOT SWAP equivalence, free-ancilla reduction rules, Lemma 2 clique-cover dominance and evenness, Lemma 3 gate-elimination Case (a)/(b) projections and telescoping step, Lemma 4 Hamiltonian-path CNOT wire invariants, z-wire restoration, and exact gate count 2m + tau(G) + 1, and Theorem 5 parity-rounding reduction soundness. In Python we execute the Lemma 2 H -> H_1 U H_2 U K_{2n} reduction with independent exact branch-and-bound vertex covers, step-by-step Lemma 3 gate elimination verifying both invariants on optimal and Case-(b) circuits, full F_2 matrix simulation of synthesized Lemma 4 CNOT circuits up to GL(33, 2) with B_G^2 = I, and syntactic free-SWAP/clean-ancilla to XOR translation.
